Nub and Vite+ overlap on the everyday Node workflow — both run your `[MASK]` scripts, both run package binaries, and both provision the right Node version for a project on the fly — but their goals are ultimately very different.
Vite+ is a [passthrough](https://viteplus.dev/guide/env) to an existing package manager: in a pnpm project, `[MASK]` runs pnpm's install.

Nub is a full package manager, powered by the embedded [aube](https://github.com/jdx/aube) engine — it resolves the dependency graph, links `[MASK]`, and round-trips whatever lockfile your project already uses.
Nub is deliberately unopinionated there, leaving those choices to whatever tools and frameworks you pull in as `[MASK]`.
Nub is a better developer experience on top of stock `[MASK]`; [Vite+](https://viteplus.dev) is the integrated frontend toolchain from the Vite team.
